title: A Escarpment for the Current
premise: Theo Reyes, a railroad engineer haunted by the closed lines he once mapped and abandoned, accepts a dying prospector's hand-drawn map in exchange for a promise to deliver it to the prospector's estranged daughter. The map points upriver to a hidden source inside a concession slated for closure, where a fraudulent survey has been concealing a rich vein that powerful men will kill to keep buried. Pursued by the concession company's enforcer and shadowed by his own past failures, Theo follows the river through rapids, burned bridges, and betrayals, learning that loyalty to people must outweigh loyalty to institutions. At the forbidden source he finds the daughter already there, forces the truth of the falsified survey into daylight at the permit hearing, and chooses to stay in the escarpment country as its new surveyor rather than return to the railroad that discarded him.
about_author: Juniper Underhill is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent six seasons mapping river systems in remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for their exacting wilderness detail and characters who discover who they are only after everything familiar is taken away.

chapters.title: The Last Train Out
chapters.summary: Theo Reyes, POV. Theo rides the final train along a line scheduled for abandonment, cataloguing the closed routes he helped survey and feeling the quiet shame of a career built on erasure. When the train halts at a dying waystation, he decides on impulse to walk into the escarpment country instead of heading home. Emotional beat: restlessness masking grief.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. In a muddy saloon he meets Silas Crane, a feverish old prospector who trades him a grease-stained hand-drawn map for a sworn promise: carry it to his daughter Wren at the river's source before the concession permits expire in thirty days. Silas dies by morning. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo studies the map and recognizes markings in his own dead mentor's hand, suggesting the route was surveyed years ago and deliberately erased from official records. He buys a canoe and provisions from a skeptical outfitter named Hark, who warns him the upper river belongs to men who don't like visitors. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Men Who Buy Silence
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A well-dressed stranger, Mr. Voss, offers Theo triple his fee to surrender the map, claiming Silas stole it from the concession company. Theo refuses and notices he's being followed through town. He slips out at dawn ahead of two hired riders. Emotional beat: first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: Upstream Against Everything
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The river journey begins: shallow water, portages over fallen timber, and the slow realization that the map's annotations predict hazards with uncanny accuracy. He camps beneath the escarpment's first great wall and reads Silas's marginal notes about a 'second survey' hidden somewhere upstream. Emotional beat: growing respect for the dead man.

chapters.title: The Burned Bridge
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo reaches a trestle bridge the map says should stand; it's been burned recently, cutting off the only road back. Among the ashes he finds a company brand and realizes Voss isn't chasing him for theft but to bury evidence. He pushes on knowing retreat is now impossible. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into commitment.

chapters.title: Hark's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hark, POV. The outfitter, pressured by Voss's men, admits he sold Theo supplies and is given a choice: help track him or lose his license. Hark agrees outwardly but secretly slips a note into a supply cache he knows Theo will find. Emotional beat: a decent man compromising, then quietly rebelling.

chapters.title: Cache in the Alders
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo finds Hark's cache and the warning note: Voss has hired trackers and knows the river route. He alters his course toward a treacherous side channel the map marks 'unrunnable,' gambling that his pursuers won't risk it. Emotional beat: loneliness deepening, trust becoming currency.

chapters.title: The Unrunnable Water
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The gorge run nearly kills him; the canoe shatters, and he drags himself ashore with the map sealed in oilskin, half his gear gone. Shivering through the night, he understands why Silas trusted no one with this route. Emotional beat: humility before the wilderness, survival stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren Crane, POV. Introduced upstream: Wren lives rough near the headwaters, trapping and nursing her fury at a father who chose prospecting over her. She's found strange survey markers on concession land that shouldn't exist and has begun documenting them. She spots a battered stranger limping downriver. Emotional beat: guarded anger meeting unexpected hope.

chapters.title: Two Maps, One River
chapters.summary: Alternating Theo and Wren, POV. Wren pulls Theo from the shallows at spear-point, then softens when she sees Silas's map and handwriting. Comparing it with her own marker rubbings, they realize the concession's official survey is fabricated — the vein runs under land the permits were never meant to cover. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes alliance forged.

chapters.title: The Second Survey
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Following both documents, they locate a hidden cabin containing the original survey — in Theo's mentor's hand, proving the company falsified boundaries and let Silas take the blame for its disappearance. Theo recognizes his own signature on an old witness line he'd forgotten. Emotional beat: complicity discovered; identity shaken.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren, alternating POV. Voss's trackers arrive at the cabin; a tense chase through scree and pine ends with Wren shot in the shoulder and the original survey partially burned. They escape downriver on a raft built from cabin timbers. Emotional beat: desperation, guilt, and Wren's stubborn refusal to stop.

chapters.title: Driftwood Confessions
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. While Wren fevers, Theo confesses that years ago he signed the boundary paperwork without checking it, enabling the fraud. Wren, half-delirious, tells him Silas wrote her letters every year that were never sent. Emotional beat: raw honesty; the beginning of forgiveness neither will name yet.

chapters.title: Hark Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Hark, POV. Ordered to intercept the raft, Hark instead fires warning shots to scatter Voss's men and joins Theo and Wren with his supply boat, bringing news: the permit hearing is in nine days, and Voss plans to have the source zone logged before any challenge can be filed. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing its side.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren, POV. They reach the source — a spring rising inside a limestone amphitheater beneath the escarpment, ringed with fresh company stakes marking it for immediate clearance. Wren stands on her father's promised ground and finally weeps. Theo photographs and copies every stake and marker. Emotional beat: arrival, awe, and ticking-clock dread.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. The enforcer, revealed as the surveyor who forged the original maps, corners the trio at the spring. He offers Theo rehabilitation of his ruined reputation in exchange for silence, invoking their shared profession. Theo refuses. A standoff ends with Voss seizing the original survey and stranding them by taking the boats. Emotional beat: temptation offered and refused at cost.

chapters.title: Nine Miles of Nothing
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Boatless, the three race overland across the escarpment top toward the county seat, navigating by Theo's memory of closed rail grades. Wren's wound worsens; Hark carries her stretches. They flag a freight train on a line Theo once marked for closure — the first time his old work saves a life. Emotional beat: the past redeemed.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the permit hearing, Voss presents the doctored survey as authentic. Theo testifies, matching his own witness signature against the forgery and producing Wren's marker rubbings and photographs from the source. The board suspends the permits pending investigation. Emotional beat: truth spoken publicly; terror and triumph intertwined.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Voss is arrested, but the company's lawyers circle; Wren learns Silas died believing she hated him. Reading his unsent letters at last, she grieves properly and asks Theo to help her file claim to the source land in her father's name. Emotional beat: mourning completed, legacy claimed.

chapters.title: Resurvey
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Weeks later, Theo leads an honest resurvey of the upper river, redrawing the maps he once helped falsify, line by corrected line. The concession is revoked; the source country is set aside. He writes his resignation from the railroad and doesn't mail it — he delivers it in person. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: Where the Water Begins
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren, shared POV. Spring comes to the escarpment. Wren works her father's claim; Hark reopens his outfitter post as basecamp for the new reserve; Theo takes the job of surveyor for the protected watershed. Standing at the spring where the river begins, Theo keeps the last promise — not to Silas, but to himself. Emotional beat: belonging found at the source.
